facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Pipeline & Backdoor is the most famous wave on the planet, a heaving barrel that detonates over an uneven lava-slab reef only about 80 metres off Ehukai Beach Park on Oahu's North Shore. It's really two waves sharing one peak: Pipeline, the legendary left, and Backdoor, the super-hollow right that funnels across the shallow reef toward Off-The-Wall. Outer reefs refract and focus arriving swell onto the inside reef, so a wave that looks absent on a flat day can come roaring back to life when the right swell shows up. It's rated among the best waves in the world. Skill (surfnerd): Expert. Surf-forecast Pipeline_1: "Pipeline in Oahu is an exposed reef break that has fairly consistent surf, although summer tends to be mostly flat. The best wind direction is from the southeast. Most of the surf here comes from groundswells and the best swell direction is from the west northwest. Often Crowded. Watch out for rocks and locals." Surf-forecast Backdoor-5: "Backdoor in Oahu is an exposed reef break that has quite reliable surf, although summer tends to be mostly flat. Works best in offshore winds from the southeast. Clean groundswells prevail and the ideal swell angle is from the northwest. A popular wave that can get growded. Watch out for - Rocks." Surf-forecast Banzai-Pipelines-and-Backdoor: "Banzai Pipelines and Backdoor in Oahu is an exposed reef break that has quite reliable surf, although summer tends to be mostly flat. Offshore winds are from the east southeast. Groundswells more frequent than windswells and the best swell direction is from the northwest. Reef breaks provide lefts and rights. Good surf at all stages of the tide. Often Crowded. Beware of rips and rocks." Wannasurf pipeline: quality Totally Epic; experience Pros or kamikaze only...; wave Reef-coral, Left; swell size Starts working at 1.0m-1.5m / 3ft-5ft and holds up to 4m+ / 12ft; crowd weekday Crowded, weekend Ultra crowded. Wannasurf backdoor: quality Totally Epic; experience Experienced surfers; wave Reef-coral, Right; swell size Starts working at 1.5m-2m /5ft-6ft and holds up to 5m / 16 ft and over; crowd weekday Crowded, weekend Ultra crowded. Access (surfnerd): Ehukai Beach Park sits right in front of the break, with a car park offering free parking plus roadside parking, though spaces fill fast when the surf is good. Facilities include restrooms, showers, and lifeguards on the beach. facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Sunset isn't one wave but a whole arena of sections spread across a huge playing field of uneven reef. It's a waterman's wave, where open-ocean power unloads and surfers swap equipment and adjust their approach to suit the reef's wide variability and moody nature. The zone runs from Val's Reef and the Inside Bowl to the West Peak, The Point, and Backyards, each section breaking differently depending on the day. Both lefts and rights show up, and the water is clean, clear, and blue. Skill (surfnerd): Expert. Surf-forecast Sunset_1: "Sunset in Oahu is an exposed reef break that has very reliable surf, although summer tends to be mostly flat. The best wind direction is from the south southeast. Groundswells more frequent than windswells and the best swell direction is from the northwest. Both left and right reef breaks. It very rarely gets crowded here. Beware of rocks and locals." Surf-forecast Sunset-Point-Vals-Reef: "Sunset Point/Vals Reef in Oahu is an exposed reef break that is often working, although summer tends to be mostly flat. Offshore winds are from the south southeast. Groundswells are more common than windswells and the ideal swell angle is from the northwest. There is a right hand reef break. When it's working here, it can get crowded. Beware of rocks and locals." Wannasurf sunset_beach: quality Totally Epic; experience Experienced surfers; wave Reef-rocky, Right; swell size Starts working at 1.0m-1.5m / 3ft-5ft and holds up to 5m / 16 ft and over; crowd weekday Crowded, weekend Crowded. Access (surfnerd): Getting in is easy, with public parking along Kam Highway right at Sunset Beach and roadside parking where authorized. facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Waimea Bay is the benchmark big-wave spot on Hawaii's North Shore, a right-hander that breaks over uneven reef and has long served as a proving ground for big-wave surfers. Deep, clear outer water lets swell arrive suddenly and trip on the lava ledge off the north point, producing the famous near-freefall Waimea takeoff, a fat shoulder, and a long race to the channel. It only comes to life on serious swells, and when it does every wave carries real consequence. Skill (surfnerd): Expert. Surf-forecast Waimea-Bay-Pinballs: "Waimea Bay/Pinballs in Oahu is an exposed reef break that usually has waves, although summer tends to be mostly flat. Offshore winds blow from the east southeast. Tends to receive distant groundswells and the best swell direction is from the northwest. There is a right breaking reef. Sometimes crowded. Watch out for rips and locals." Wannasurf waimea_bay: quality Totally Epic; experience Pros or kamikaze only...; wave Point-break, Right; swell size Starts working at 1.0m-1.5m / 3ft-5ft and holds up to 5m / 16 ft and over; crowd weekday Few surfers, weekend Crowded. Access (surfnerd): Getting in and out is done through the keyhole near the rocks in the northeast corner, where the shorebreak is smallest; it needs a little timing as the size grows. There is a car park with free parking plus roadside parking, along with restrooms, showers, and a lifeguard, but parking becomes nearly impossible once the Bay is breaking and cars fill the lot and line Kam Highway, so plan to walk in from further afield. facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Laniakea, known locally as Lani's, is a broad right-breaking reef about two and a half miles north of Haleiwa on Oahu's North Shore. The main takeoff sits roughly 400 yards offshore, over one half of a massive lava hammerhead; the other half forms the left known as Jocko's, a quarter-mile to the northeast. A channel running out beside the point cuts partway through the reef, giving a fast paddler a way across the thinnest section between closeouts. On its day it ranks among the North Shore's finest waves, a long ride that offers a bit of everything. Check: surfnerd states facing NW but best swell NE (90 degrees apart); both are as published. Hazards include rocks and sharks." facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Chun's is a right-hand reef break on Oahu's North Shore, tucked between Jocko's and Waimea Bay. It breaks over uneven, often shallow and sharp reef across an elbow, throwing up both a left and a right. The right is faster but shorter and draws very shallow on the inside, while the bonus left off the middle runs shoulderier and more forgiving as it spills into deeper water. Its three sections, the outside, middle, and bowl, each offer roll-ins, workable walls, and the odd tube, and it can turn hollow and fast when it's on. Skill (surfnerd): Beginner. Surf-forecast Chuns-Reef: "Chuns Reef in Oahu is an exposed reef break that has very reliable surf, although summer tends to be mostly flat. Works best in offshore winds from the southeast. Most of the surf here comes from groundswells and the ideal swell angle is from the north. The quality of the surf isn't affected by the tide. Likely to be crowded if working. Hazards include - Rocks." Surf-forecast Chuns-and-Jocks-Reefs: "Chuns and Jocks Reefs in Oahu is an exposed reef break that is usually a safe bet, although summer tends to be mostly flat. Offshore winds blow from the east southeast. Tends to receive distant groundswells and the best swell direction is from the northwest. Both left and right reef breaks. The quality of the surf isn't affected by the tide. Likely to be crowded if working. Hazards include rocks/rips." Wannasurf chuns_reef: quality Regional Classic; experience Experienced surfers; wave Reef-rocky, Right and left; swell size Starts working at Less than 1m / 3ft and holds up to 2m+ / 6ft+; crowd weekday Crowded, weekend Crowded. facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Rockpile sits between Log Cabins and Off-The-Wall, breaking right in front of the pile of rocks that gives it its name. It's a big, powerful left running over uneven reef, and it can be tricky to catch at its best. When it's on, though, it throws a powerful big-wave face that can barrel. Skill (surfnerd): Expert. Surf-forecast Rockpiles-Logcabins: "Rockpiles/Logcabins in Oahu is an exposed reef break that has fairly consistent surf, although summer tends to be mostly flat. Offshore winds blow from the east southeast. Tends to receive distant groundswells and the ideal swell direction is from the northwest. There are left and right breaking reefs. It very rarely gets crowded here. Beware of rips and rocks." Access (surfnerd): There's a lifeguard on hand, and you can use the car park with free parking or find roadside parking along the highway where authorized. facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Off-The-Wall, also known as Kodak Reef, is a reef break sitting just west of Backdoor and Pipeline. It breaks over an uneven slab of reef as a wedging right, with smaller lefts peeling back toward Backdoor. On the right wave it throws a clean, almond-shaped barrel, running hollow and fast when it's on. This is an expert-only wave, and the rides tend to be short and punchy rather than long. Skill (surfnerd): Expert. Surf-forecast Offthe-Wall-Insanities: "Off the Wall/Insanities in Oahu is an exposed reef break that has quite reliable surf, although summer tends to be mostly flat. Offshore winds are from the east. Tends to receive distant groundswells and the ideal swell direction is from the northwest. Reef breaks provide lefts and rights. Best around mid tide. It's often crowded here. Hazards include urchins, rips and rocks." facts.name: Turtle Bay West
facts.windOffshore: SSE (surfnerd wind exposure ESE - SSW, "Offshore from SSE")
facts.tide: Low, Mid, High (surfnerd)
facts.season: Autumn, Winter, Spring (surfnerd)
facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Turtle Bay West is a mellow reef break on the eastern edge of Kawela Bay, with the right peeling in the shadow of the Turtle Bay Resort. It handles both rights and lefts over a reef of lava and coral, and the water here is clean and strikingly clear. Once a quiet escape from the North Shore crush, it has become a genuine winter hotspot, and while it stays mellow by North Shore standards, it can turn really good when the swell and wind line up. Don't confuse it with Turtle Bay East, which sits around the peninsula on the resort's east side. Skill (surfnerd): Beginner, Intermediate, Expert. Access (surfnerd): Parking is easy and close to the break.

facts.name: Kaena Point
facts.windOffshore: ESE (surfnerd wind exposure ENE - SSE, "Offshore from ESE"); East-northeast (surf-forecast)
facts.tide: Low, Mid, High (surfnerd)
hazards: Respect the hazards, which include large waves, strong current, sharks, and the reef itself. (surfnerd)
facts.season: Autumn, Winter, Spring (surfnerd); Winter, most often January (surf-forecast)
facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Kaena Point is the westernmost tip of Oahu, a torrential convergence zone where North and South Pacific swell energy collides with spectacular force. It breaks over reef and rock, with lava and coral in the mix, and throws both rights and lefts as a reef and point setup. On the big N or NW swells that light it up, it stacks giant righthanders around the west side of the island and careens them down along the southern edge of the headland. Further down the point sits Yokohama Bay, where the waves run a touch tamer but can still reach serious, heavy proportions. This is expert-only terrain. Skill (surfnerd): Expert. Surf-forecast Kaena-Point: "Kaena Point in Oahu is an exposed reef break that usually has waves and can work at any time of the year. Works best in offshore winds from the east northeast. Groundswells more frequent than windswells and the ideal swell angle is from the west northwest.. Rarely crowded here. Hazards include rips, rocks and locals." Access (surfnerd): Walk in on the Kaena Point Trail, either from the north or from Yokohama Bay in the south. Other guide pins from this position: surf-forecast Kaena-Point 1.0 km.

Fast, thumping lefts and just as angry rights break over a mosaic of live coral heads, and it takes speed to get in and race the section cleanly. facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Tracks is a long reef with a sandy inside in Kahe Beach Park, breaking over dead coral close to the shore. It throws both lefts and rights: the lefts show up on south to southwest swells, while punchy rights fire on north to northwest swells. The main peak sits down near the power plant, producing electric rights and longer lefts, and a handful of lesser peaks stretch north toward Nanakuli. With everything breaking so close in, it is also a great spot to watch the action. Skill (surfnerd): Beginner. Surf-forecast Nanakuli-Tracks: "Nanakuli Tracks in Oahu is an exposed reef break that has unreliable waves with no particular seasonal pattern. Works best in offshore winds from the east northeast. Most of the surf here comes from groundswells and the optimum swell angle is from the southwest. Good surf at all stages of the tide. The location means that it never gets crowded. Watch out for - Urchins - Rocks - Localism - Sharks." Surf-forecast Tracks-Nanakuli: "Tracks(Nanakuli) in Oahu is an exposed beach and reef break that has consistent surf and can work at any time of the year. Offshore winds are from the northeast. Groundswells more frequent than windswells and the ideal swell angle is from the west. A choice of left and right reefs. Sometimes crowded. Take care of sharks,." facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Kahuku, also known as 7th Hole, sits off the 7th hole of the Kahuku Golf Course at the start of the Windward Side, just around the bend from the North Shore. It's a reef break that offers both a powerful left and right, split by a deep channel that's often sharky. When a solid northeast swell lines up with offshore winds from a passing front, it's one of the best spots on the Windward Side, with long rides and barrels, though catching it that good isn't all that common. Skill (surfnerd): Beginner, Intermediate, Expert. Access (surfnerd): Cross the golf course at or near the 7th hole to reach the break. It's a long paddle out, though you get to use the channel, and the long rides mean long paddles back. When the spot's working, you'll figure out the way easily enough.

The main draw is a racey, hollow right that peels toward Kahana Bay, and tube-riding skills are essential when it's on. There are also some lefts on the far side of the reef outcrop, though they tend to be short. The wave breaks over lava, rock, and coral. Skill (surfnerd): Beginner, Intermediate, Expert. Surf-forecast Crouching-Lion: "Crouching Lion in Oahu is an exposed point break that has unreliable waves with no particular seasonal pattern. The best wind direction is from the south southwest. Access (surfnerd): Getting in is easy, but there's a long paddle out to the break. It sits in a channel, which helps, though the long rides mean long paddles back. The beach break provides left and right handers. Sometimes crowded. Watch out for rocks/crowds." facts.season: Summer, most often May (surf-forecast)
facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Ala Moana Bowls is one of the best waves on Oahu, a long, barreling reef that peels outside the Ala Wai Harbor. It owes its shape to dredging: a deepwater channel was cut so boats could reach the harbour, and south swell refracts out of that channel and wedges up along the reef. Expect big, round curves as the wave bowls over sections of reef, shoulders off, then gathers into another barrel on the shallow inside. It breaks both left and right over live coral. Surfnerd has 2 entries for this break with different stated facings (ala-moana-bowls=SSW, ala-moana-bowls-hawaii=SW); seaward uses the primary entry (ala-moana-bowls), both kept. Second Surfnerd entry https://www.surfnerd.com/surf-forecast/ala-moana-bowls-hawaii: workable swell SSE - WSW , offshore None, 2ft - 10ft, Lava, Rock, Coral, Reef, Right, Left, Low, Mid, High, Intermediate, Expert, Spring, Summer, Autumn, Shortboard, Bodyboard, Funboard, Longboard, Fish. Skill (surfnerd): Expert. Surf-forecast Ala-Moana-Bowls: "Ala Moana Bowls in Oahu is an exposed reef break that has pretty consitent surf. Summer offers the favoured conditions for surfing. Offshore winds blow from the north. Most of the surf here comes from groundswells and the best swell direction is from the south southeast. Both left and right reef breaks. The quality of the surf isn't affected by the tide. Likely to be crowded if working. Beware of urchins, rocks, obstacles, locals and pollution." Wannasurf ala_moana_bowls: quality World Class; experience Experienced surfers; wave Reef-coral, Right and left; swell size Starts working at Less than 1m / 3ft and holds up to 5m / 16 ft and over; crowd weekday Few surfers, weekend Ultra crowded. Access (surfnerd): Paddle out from Magic Island when it's big, or straight into the channel when it's small. Be ready for a long paddle and plenty of hazards: currents sweeping the channel, large sharks, boat traffic, sharp coral reef, urchins, and the rusty remnants of an old navigation pole. There's a surf shop nearby, and parking is paid and can be expensive, with metered, roadside, car park, and restricted options around. facts.windOffshore: NE (surfnerd wind exposure N - E, "Offshore from NE")

facts.season: Spring, Summer, Autumn (surfnerd)
facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: South Shore - Ala Moana Park isn't a single break but a cluster of good reef waves packed into about a half-mile of coast. From east to west you'll find Kaisers, Rockpiles, Ala Moana Bowls, and Magic Island, each with its own character, from rights and lefts to barrels and bowls. The reef serves up consistently fun surf across all of them, so you can pick the peak that suits your session. Skill (surfnerd): Intermediate, Expert. Access (surfnerd): You can reach any of the spots from the breakwater and channels, or paddle straight out from the small beach beside the Ala Moana parking lot across the shallow reef platform, which gets a little sketchy at low tide. The paddles to and from the beach can be long, but it eases off once you're outside. Keep in mind the reef is shallow and sharp, and the nearby harbor means pollution is a factor, especially after heavy rain.

facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Kaisers is the easternmost break on the Ala Moana reef, a steep, fast, bowly right that peels over a shallow live-coral bottom. It throws a good barrel section off the peak and is fun to backdoor, and because the right spills into a channel you get an easy paddle back out. There is also a left, usually a little more slopey, that tends to close out on the inside. It is an expert-level reef break, and when everything lines up it is one of the better waves in the area. Skill (surfnerd): Expert. Surf-forecast Kaisers: "Kaisers in Oahu is an exposed reef break that has dependable surf. Summer offers the favoured conditions for surfing. Ideal winds are from the north. Windswells and groundswells in equal measure and the best swell direction is from the south southeast. The reef provides both left and right breaks. Good surf at all stages of the tide. Sometimes crowded. Watch out for rocks, obstacles, locals and sharks." Wannasurf kaisers: quality Regional Classic; experience Experienced surfers; wave Reef-coral, Right and left; swell size Starts working at Less than 1m / 3ft and holds up to 2.5m+ / 8ft+; crowd weekday Few surfers, weekend Ultra crowded. Access (surfnerd): There is plenty on hand nearby, including restrooms, showers, a lifeguard, a surf school, and a surf shop. Parking is paid, metered, or roadside with a car park available, and it can get tricky around the harbour. To get out, walk the east breakwater by the Ala Moana parking lot to the end and paddle out through the channel, or paddle from the little beach near the parking lot across the reef platform, which is a bit sketchy at low tide. It's a peak with a decent right that peels and swings down the line, throwing up a few bowly sections toward the inside, alongside a shorter, mushier left. Most days it's a mellow, user-friendly wave, but it can really come alive when a solid swell is running. The bottom is dead coral reef, so keep that in mind. Skill (surfnerd): Intermediate. facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Publics is one of the longest, most consistent lefts in the Waikiki area, peeling along the fringe of reef on the east flank of the bay. The lines look easy and inviting, but the wave breaks over shallow, live coral, and the fingers of reef reaching up from the bottom make it a spot for surfers who know what they are doing. High tide leaves the wave a little mushy but safer, while low tide sharpens it into a racier ride with the occasional tube section, along with a real chance of losing some skin on the reef. Offshore winds are from the north northeast with some shelter here from east winds. Groundswells and windswells are equally likely and the best swell direction is from the south southeast. There is a left hand reef break. Surfable at all stages of the tide. Watch out for rocks,etc." Access (surfnerd): Getting in from land is easy: park at Sans Souci State Recreational Park, with free, paid, and roadside options nearby, plus showers on hand. facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Honolua Bay is a world-class right-hand pointbreak set in a cliff-lined amphitheatre on Maui's northwest coast, and it ranks among the best waves on the planet. The right peels over an uneven reef through a series of barrel and turn sections that can run for the better part of a quarter-mile. Surfers break it down by zone: Coconuts is the outermost takeoff with the most size, Outside stands up into the first hollow wall, Cave delivers the thickest and most high-performance barrels, and the inside Keiki Bowl finishes racy over shallow reef. facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Peahi - Jaws is Maui's most notorious wave, a big-wave reef that most surfers will only ever watch. It broke into wider view in the early 1990s as tow-in surfing developed, and it has held its biggest-and-baddest reputation ever since, supplying a string of XXL award winners over the years. The wave breaks over an uneven reef and is famous above all for its perfect, house-sized right-hand tubes. Surfnerd lists this break twice (peahi-jaws, peahi-jaws-hawaii); merged, same facing. Second Surfnerd entry https://www.surfnerd.com/surf-forecast/peahi-jaws-hawaii: workable swell NW - NE , offshore None, 20ft - 50ft, Lava, Rock, Coral, Reef, Point, Offshore, Right, Left, Low, Mid, High, Expert, Autumn, Winter, Spring, Gun, Tow. Skill (surfnerd): Expert. Surf-forecast Jaws: "Jaws in Maui is an exposed reef break that has fairly consistent surf. Winter is the best time of year for surfing here. The best wind direction is from the south southwest. Groundswells are more common than windswells and the best swell direction is from the north northeast. Reef breaks provide lefts and rights. The quality of the surf isn't affected by the tide. Even when there are waves, it's not likley to be crowded. Hazards include rips and rocks." Wannasurf jaws: quality Totally Epic; experience Pros or kamikaze only...; wave Reef-rocky, Right; swell size Starts working at Over 3.5m / 12ft and holds up to 5m / 16 ft and over; crowd weekday Empty, weekend Empty. Access (surfnerd): Getting out is done by launching at Maliko Gulch, where punching in and out of the closed-out bay is a gamble in itself. If you just want to see it, drive out to Peahi, park on the western headland, and find a comfortable spot on the cliff above the break. Bring binoculars and a long lens. When kona winds blow, both Kanaha and the better reefs up at Sprecklesville can clean up into picture-perfect left and right walls with the odd tube. Surfnerd lists this break twice (kanaha, kanaha-hawaii); merged, same facing. Second Surfnerd entry https://www.surfnerd.com/surf-forecast/kanaha-hawaii: workable swell NW - ENE , offshore None, 3ft - 10ft, Lava, Rock, Coral, Reef, Right, Left, Low, Mid, High, Beginner, Intermediate, Autumn, Winter, Spring, Shortboard, Funboard, Longboard, Fish, Bodyboard, Kiteboard. Skill (surfnerd): Intermediate. Surf-forecast Kanaha: "Kanaha in Maui is an exposed reef break that has quite reliable surf. Winter is the best time of year for surfing here. Works best in offshore winds from the southeast. Most of the surf here comes from groundswells and the best swell direction is from the north northeast. Good surf at all stages of the tide. A fairly popluar wave that can sometimes get crowded Watch out for - Sharks." facts.season: Autumn, Winter, Spring (surfnerd); Winter, most often December (surf-forecast)
facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Kahului Harbor sits on the north-central coast of Maui and is a genuinely fun place to score, with several breaks firing inside and outside the harbor. The standout is the right on the west side. When a large swell pushes through the wide entrance, energy refracts out of the deeper channel and crosses up with swell bouncing off the jetty, stacking into a powerful roll-in wedge over shallow water. It is a mini-Box-style wedge that rewards surfers and bodyboarders who can handle abrupt steps and throw into barrels. There is a left off the same peak, but it dumps straight into the deep channel and does not offer much. Treat it as more of a novelty than a world-beater, though it is a blast when it turns on. Skill (surfnerd): Intermediate, Expert. Surf-forecast Kahului-Harbor: "Kahului Harbor in Maui is an exposed reef break that has consistent surf. Winter is the favoured time of year for surfing here. Offshore winds are from the south with some shelter here from east winds. Clean groundswells prevail and the best swell direction is from the north northeast. Reef breaks provide lefts and rights. Good surf at all stages of the tide. When the surf is up, it can get quite busy in the water. Beware of urchins, rips, rocks, locals, pollution and sharks." Wannasurf kahului_harbor: quality Totally Epic; experience Pros or kamikaze only...; wave Reef-rocky, Right and left; swell size Starts working at Less than 1m / 3ft and holds up to 3m+ / 10ft+; crowd weekday Few surfers, weekend Few surfers. Access (surfnerd): Getting there is easy: park at the harbor and jump in right at the lineup. The paddle out is straightforward, though the current can make it tough to hold your position once you are in the spot. Keep in mind you are surfing inside a working harbor with noticeable pollution, and watch for the shallow bottom on the right wedge, urchins, rocks, sharks, and shifting rips. Other guide pins from this position: surf-forecast Kahului-Harbor 1.7 km, wannasurf kahului_harbor 1.4 km.

facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Hana Bay sits on the far eastern edge of Maui, in the town of Hana. A reef off each side of the bay shelters it from most swells, so it takes the right setup to break. Access (surfnerd): Getting out is easy, with a short paddle from just about anywhere in the bay, and Hana Beach Park sits on the southern end. facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: La Perouse Bay is a very rocky bay tucked into the desolate, beautiful southern corner of Maui, and it serves up powerful, clean lefts. The break sits over a mix of lava, rock, and coral in a pristine setting. On its day it delivers a long, workable left, though the shoulders can turn slopey and fat. Skill (surfnerd): Intermediate, Expert. Surf-forecast La-Perouse-Bay-The-Dumps: "La Perouse Bay/The Dumps in Maui is a reasonably exposed reef break that only works once in a while. Summer offers the best conditions for surfing. Offshore winds are from the north northeast. Groundswells and windswells are equally likely and the best swell direction is from the south. A left hand reef break. Sometimes crowded. Watch out for rocks." Wannasurf la_perouse_bay: quality Normal; experience Experienced surfers; wave Reef-rocky, Left; swell size Starts working at 1.5m-2m /5ft-6ft and holds up to 5m / 16 ft and over; crowd weekday Empty, weekend Few surfers. Access (surfnerd): The road leads right down to the bay, though you may need a 4WD depending on current road conditions. Getting in and out over the rocky beach can be tricky, especially on a solid, consistent swell. Watch for shallow reef, strong currents, and the occasional shark sighting. facts.name: Kaiolohia Bay/Shipwreck Beach
facts.windOffshore: SSW (surfnerd wind exposure SSE - WSW, "Offshore from SSW")
facts.tide: Low, Mid, High (surfnerd)
hazards: Watch for reef, sharks, current, and the genuine risk of getting lost along this remote coast. (surfnerd)
facts.season: Autumn, Winter, Spring (surfnerd)
facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Kaiolohia Bay, also known as Shipwreck Beach, is an 8-mile stretch of windswept coastline on the north side of Lanai, about a half-hour drive from Lanai City. It faces the Kalohi Channel, the shallow, 10-mile band of sea separating Lanai and Molokai. The sheer scale of the place means plenty of reefs to choose from, all breaking roughly 500 to 600 yards offshore over lava, rock, and coral. It stays pristine and largely empty, and the peaks throw both rights and lefts. Skill (surfnerd): Beginner, Intermediate, Expert. Access (surfnerd): Getting here means dirt roads only, so a 4x4 is a must.

facts.tide: Low, Mid (surfnerd); There is a right hand reef break Good surf at all stages of the tide. (surf-forecast); All tides, Rising and falling tides (wannasurf)

facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Hanalei Bay is the heart of surfing on Kauai, and its main draw is a long right-hand point that peels along the eastern side of the bay for up to 300 yards over lava reef. It's a powerful wave with occasional barrel sections, and the ride finishes on an inside bowl section in the middle of the bay. The reef here is live coral. Check: surfnerd states facing W but best swell N (90 degrees apart); both are as published. Skill (surfnerd): Beginner. Surf-forecast Hanalei-Bay: "Hanalei Bay in Kauai is an exposed reef and point break that has consistent surf, although summer tends to be mostly flat. The best wind direction is from the south southeast. Tends to receive distant groundswells and the optimum swell angle is from the north. There is a right hand reef break Good surf at all stages of the tide. A popular wave that can get growded. Beware of locals and sharks." Wannasurf hanalei_bay: quality World Class; experience Experienced surfers; wave None, Right; swell size Starts working at 1.0m-1.5m / 3ft-5ft and holds up to 5m / 16 ft and over; crowd weekday Crowded, weekend Ultra crowded. Access (surfnerd): Getting in is easy: paddle out from the Hanalei Pier area, or from the keyhole off Puu Poa Beach, midway along the point. The paddle is long but not difficult, and since it's a point break, a longer ride means a longer paddle back. You'll find restrooms and showers, along with roadside parking and a car park. facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Brenneckes is a beach break on Kauai's Poipu coast, throwing up lefts and rights over a mix of uneven reef and sand. The tight cove holds punchy peaks, but it's a bodyboarding-only spot, so anyone hoping to stand up should look at the neighboring Poipu Beach breaks instead. Inside Waiohai is a sucky peak that comes alive on higher tide, while First Break serves up outside reef action best left to experts. Beginners can slide over to Lemon Drops for rolling walls over rock and sand. Skill (surfnerd): Beginner. Surf-forecast Brenneckes: "Brenneckes in Kauai is an exposed reef break that has reasonably consistent surf. Summer offers the best conditions for surfing. Offshore winds are from the north northeast. Waves just as likely from local windswells as from distant groundswells and the best swell direction is from the south. Both left and right reef breaks. Surfable at all stages of the tide. It's sometimes crowded here. Beware of urchins, rips and rocks." Other guide pins from this position: surf-forecast Brenneckes 1.2 km.

facts.name: Poipu Outer Reef
facts.windOffshore: NNE (surfnerd wind exposure NNW - ENE, "Offshore from NNE")
facts.tide: Mid, High (surfnerd)
hazards: Keep the shallow reef and the chance of sharks in mind before you paddle out. (surfnerd)

facts.season: Spring, Summer, Autumn (surfnerd)
facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Poipu Outer Reef is a heavy, expert-level reef break on Kauai's south shore, throwing a shallow left barrel alongside a longer, more sloped right. The bottom is a mix of rock, coral and lava sitting very shallow, so it demands respect and rewards experience. Mellower, more popular waves break closer to the beach at Lemon Drops and Waiohai, and heading west past Poipu you'll find PKs, Centers, Heroins and Acid Drop, each with its own mood but all carrying the same shallow-reef risk. Skill (surfnerd): Expert. Access (surfnerd): Paddle straight out to the outside reef from Kiahuna Beach, where there's also a parking lot. Be ready for a long paddle, and note that currents can get bad at times.

facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Kahalu'u Bay is a mellow reef break with a handful of rolling peaks to choose from, breaking over a mix of lava, rock, and coral. Most of the time it serves up forgiving rights and lefts that suit beginners, but when a solid swell fills in, the outermost peak turns on with a semi-steep drop and rippable lines that keep intermediate surfers busy. Hazards include - Urchins - Rips / undertow - Rocks - Localism." Beware of urchins, rips, rocks and locals." facts.name: La'aloa Beach Park
facts.windOffshore: ENE (surfnerd wind exposure NNE - ESE, "Offshore from ENE"); E (surfnerd guide text: "east (E) offshore wind")
facts.tide: Low, Mid, High (surfnerd)
facts.season: Spring, Summer, Autumn, Winter (surfnerd)
facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: La'aloa Beach Park, better known as Magic Sands or White Sands, is a rare Big Island beachbreak whose true Hawaiian name means "very sacred." It earns its Disappearing Sands nickname during large winter swells between December and March, when the golden bay-shore sand washes out to sea overnight and leaves bare lava rock behind. That happens because a deep, sand-bottomed scoop in the reef runs straight out to deep water just offshore. Skill (surfnerd): Beginner. Access (surfnerd): Getting in is easy, with free parking at La'aloa Beach Park and roadside spots along Ali'i Drive. It's a very short paddle out, and you'll find restrooms and a lifeguard on hand.

Surf-forecast Keawaiki-Bay: "Keawaiki Bay in Big Island is a reasonably exposed beach and reef break that has reliable surf. Winter is the best time of year for surfing here. The best wind direction is from the east southeast. Groundswells are more common than windswells and the best swell direction is from the northwest. Reef breaks provide lefts and rights. Sometimes crowded. Beware of rips and sharks." Access (surfnerd): There is free roadside parking near the highway, but reaching the water takes some effort. Plan on a trek in from the road, or the walk along the Kings Highway Foot Trail. The pay-off is a nice beach to hang out on once you have made it down. facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Waipio Valley is a black-sand beachbreak that finally cuts some relief into the long, cliff-lined stretch of the Hamakua Coast. Rivermouth flow carves the sandbars into lefts and rights separated by clean channels, and the peaks are forgiving enough for beginners while still holding fun waves for stronger surfers. Everything breaks over sand. Skill (surfnerd): Beginner. Surf-forecast Waipio-Valley: "Waipio Valley in Big Island is an exposed river break that has fairly consistent surf and can work at any time of the year. Offshore winds are from the south southwest. Tends to receive distant groundswells and the best swell direction is from the north. The quality of the surf isn't affected by the tide. When it's working here, it can get crowded. Take care of - Rips / undertow - Rocks - Localism - Sharks." Access (surfnerd): Getting in is the catch: the road down is 4WD-only or a long walk on foot, and parking is restricted. facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Pohoiki is a lava-reef spot with three separate bays, each offering a different wave over an uneven reef. The bottom is extremely sharp lava rock dotted with urchins, so it pays to avoid contact at all times. The three bays give you options. First Bay sits closest to the boat ramp, with a wave that suits all levels and warm water from nearby volcanic springs. Second Bay lies a little further out in slightly cooler water and throws a more hollow, faster wave for advanced surfers. Third Bay, around a small rocky outcrop to the south, is hollow and fast over shallow water, and can turn into a solid big-wave spot when a strong swell meets west-to-north wind. Check: surfnerd states facing SSE but best swell NE (112.5 degrees apart); both are as published. Skill (surfnerd): Intermediate. Surf-forecast Pohoiki: "Pohoiki in Big Island is an exposed reef break that has pretty consitent surf and can work at any time of the year. Works best in offshore winds from the west northwest. Windswells and groundswells in equal measure and the ideal swell angle is from the east. Both left and right reef breaks. When it's working here, it can get crowded. Take care of urchins, rocks, locals and sharks." Wannasurf pohiki: quality Regional Classic; experience All surfers; wave Reef-rocky, Right and left; swell size Starts working at 1.0m-1.5m / 3ft-5ft and holds up to; crowd weekday Few surfers, weekend Crowded. Access (surfnerd): Getting in is easy, with parking at Isaac Hale Beach Park. Other guide pins from this position: surf-forecast Pohoiki 3.1 km, wannasurf pohiki 0.6 km.

facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Lahaina Breakwall is a reef break at Lahaina Harbor on the west coast of Maui. This side of the island sits in the swell shadow of Moloka'i, Lana'i and Kaho'olawe, so finding surf here often takes patience, yet the harbor breakwater manages to pull in waves all year long. Depending on the swell, it can serve up either a quality left or a quality right, both capable of barreling and holding open. Skill (surfnerd): Intermediate. Surf-forecast Lahaina-Harbor-Break-Wall: "Lahaina Harbor Break Wall in Maui is a fairly exposed reef break that has very reliable surf and works all around the year. Offshore winds blow from the northeast. Clean groundswells prevail and the ideal swell direction is from the southwest. It's often crowded here. Beware of - Urchins - Rocks." Surf-forecast Lahaina-Breakwall-Harbour: "Lahaina Breakwall/Harbour in Maui is a quite exposed reef break that usually has waves and can work at any time of the year. Works best in offshore winds from the northeast. Tends to receive distant groundswells and the ideal swell angle is from the west southwest. A choice of left and right reefs. Sometimes crowded. Watch out for rocks,urchins,boats." Access (surfnerd): Getting out is easy, straight off the breakwall at the harbor. The paddle isn't too bad, though currents can pick up on solid swells. Watch for the reef, along with urchins and sharp coral, and keep in mind that the harbor water is often suspect. facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Little Beach, also known as Pu'u Ola'i Beach, sits on the southern end of Maui right next to Big Beach, a scenic cove that mostly serves up shorepound. Most days it is skimboarding, bodysurfing, and bodyboarding territory, with beach break that can turn sizeable and strong and throw closeout barrels. On bigger, longer-period swells a surfboard option can open up off the rocks on the sides of the cove. It is also the only generally accepted clothing-optional beach on Maui. Skill (surfnerd): Beginner, Intermediate, Expert. Surf-forecast Little-Beach-1: "Little Beach in Maui is a quite exposed reef break that only works once in a while. Summer offers the best conditions for surfing. Ideal winds are from the east northeast. Waves just as likely from local windswells as from distant groundswells and the optimum swell angle is from the south southwest. Often Crowded. Take care of - Urchins - Rips / undertow - Rocks - Localism - Sharks." Wannasurf little_beach: quality Normal; experience Experienced surfers; wave Reef-coral, Right and left; swell size Starts working at 1.0m-1.5m / 3ft-5ft and holds up to 5m / 16 ft and over; crowd weekday Crowded, weekend Ultra crowded. Access (surfnerd): Getting in is easy, off Makena Road at Makena State Park. Other guide pins from this position: surf-forecast Little-Beach-1 0.1 km, wannasurf little_beach 0.1 km.

facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Lopa Beach is a long, white-sand beach on the east coast of Lanai, with a stretch of reef just offshore that serves up a variety of peaks and sections. The reef breaks both right and left over lava, rock, and coral, and there's enough on offer for surfers of every ability. It's a pristine setting, though this rates as a below-average spot overall: it can get genuinely fun when swell and wind line up, but that combination doesn't come together all that often. Access (surfnerd): Getting here takes some effort: Lopa Beach is only reachable via 4X4-only dirt roads that branch off Keomuku Road, so a regular vehicle won't cut it. Mind the reef beneath you.

facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Pakala, also known as Pakalas, is a long, powerful left that wraps and barrels around the point on the south side of the bay. It is fast and at its best on an overhead swell, when the wave stands up and runs down the point. The lower the tide, the hollower it gets, though the bottom is coral reef, so it pays to be careful. On weaker swells it turns mellower and far less hollow, making for a more relaxed surf. Skill (surfnerd): Intermediate, Expert. Surf-forecast Pakalas: "Pakalas in Kauai is an exposed reef and point break that has pretty consitent surf. Summer offers the best conditions for surfing. Ideal winds are from the north northeast. Waves just as likely from local windswells as from distant groundswells and the ideal swell direction is from the south.Surfers ride left hand point. Surfable at all stages of the tide. It's sometimes crowded here. Beware of urchins, rips and rocks." Wannasurf pakala: quality World Class; experience All surfers; wave Reef-coral, Left; swell size Starts working at Less than 1m / 3ft and holds up to 1m+ / 3ft+; crowd weekday Ultra crowded, weekend Ultra crowded. Access (surfnerd): Pakala is tricky to spot, as you can't easily see it from the road. The easiest way to find it is to follow the cars parked along the side of the road. facts.name: Majors Bay
facts.swellExposure: SSE to WSW, W to NNW (surfnerd)
facts.windOffshore: ENE (surfnerd wind exposure NNE - ESE, "Offshore from ENE"); E (surfnerd guide text: "east (E) offshore wind"); Northeast (surf-forecast)
facts.tide: Low, Mid, High (surfnerd)
hazards: The surf here is all about rights, and the whole stretch is known for serious power and terrifying rips, where a single long ride can turn into a long walk back down the beach. (surfnerd)

Local Tips This is an expert-level wave that rewards surfers comfortable with power and current. (surfnerd)
facts.season: Autumn, Winter, Spring, Summer (surfnerd); Summer, most often August (surf-forecast)
facts.notes: Surfnerd overview: Majors Bay is a powerful, exposed break on the long, empty west coast of Kauai. It faces open ocean and pulls in energy from both the North and South Pacific, so there's swell potential across autumn, winter, spring, and summer. The surf here is all about rights, and the whole stretch is known for serious power and terrifying rips, where a single long ride can turn into a long walk back down the beach. Strong currents and the chance of sharks come with the territory. Check: surfnerd states facing WSW but best swell N (112.5 degrees apart); both are as published. Skill (surfnerd): Expert. Surf-forecast Majors-Bay: "Majors Bay in Kauai is an exposed beach and point break that has quite consistent surf and can work at any time of the year. Works best in offshore winds from the northeast. Tends to receive distant groundswells and the best swell direction is from the south. The beach breaks offers right-handers When it's working here, it can get crowded. Dangerous rips are a hazard of surfing here." Access (surfnerd): Getting to the water is easy: pull off the road, walk onto the beach almost anywhere, find a good peak, and paddle out. The standout north-swell right runs down the reef at the end of the runway, though, and that one sits on the military missile range and needs an access pass. Paddles can be short and quick when it's small, and long and tiring when it's big and consistent. The water is pristine most of the time, turning murky only after heavy rains push farmland runoff into the lineup. Other guide pins from this position: surf-forecast Majors-Bay 2.1 km.
